data.narrative:
Arbe Robotics operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector as a public-stage company that has raised $118M to date. The comparable universe consists of seven private-stage peers, including Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Zipline, Nuro, and Elroy Air, with no public peers identified in the same narrow segment. This composition—zero public comps and a small private peer set—materially constrains traditional valuation triangulation.

Peer-median analysis proved inapplicable due to insufficient clustering within tightly defined cohorts. The sector contains five same-sector peers overall, but filtering by stage, adjacency, and valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints in any meaningful bucket. The standard requirement of three or more comparable observations to establish a reliable median could not be met without resorting to all-sector aggregation, which would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of business models and maturity stages across Drones & Autonomous.

This analysis underscores the core valuation challenge: Arbe lacks both public market benchmarks and a sufficiently dense private peer cohort to support conventional multiples-based approaches. Forward-looking valuation of this company would require alternative methodologies—DCF analysis, venture capital method, or scenario-weighted approaches—rather than reliance on peer comparables. The frontier-stage and sector-specific nature of operations argues for fundamental cash flow modeling and explicit uncertainty quantification over market-based proxies.
